notes: No breadboard is used; three female-to-female jumper wires connect the PIR pins directly to the Pi header. The catalogue has no female-to-female jumper, so a new type jumper-wire-ff was added.
The diagram shows the GND wire on the Pi's physical pin 6, which is the first ground pin, so it is mapped to GND.1. The tutorial only requires 'a ground pin'.
The 5V wire goes to the pin in the top row next to the 3V3 label (physical pin 2), mapped to 5V.1.

The diagram places 5V on the red wire, GND on the black wire and GPIO4 on the orange wire. The wire colours and the order of the PIR pins (VCC, OUT, GND) are taken from the manual's text and image. GPIO 4 was chosen by the manual as an example, and any GPIO pin would work.
